name: Before Names
sub: creation myths, as each people tells them, and the one that is not a myth
preface:
Six tellings of what was before the Breath, in six hands, and none of them at my fire.

The Articles came off the lesson-board at Nine Stairs, where a sweeper let me stand with a lamp one night in my ninth winter there and did not ask what I was copying, and did not stop me copying what had been scratched under the rule.

The stair-litany was the Gold Bell's; a novice copied it for me from the leaves they keep under the stone on the top step, the summer before the Peak fell, all but one word, and told me so, and I have not been able to ask her since whether the stone is still there.

The Brood's scratching I took myself off the second landing of the Ziggurat with charcoal and a wet cloth, lying on my side in the mud, and I have kept the lower-case as it was cut, because the hand that cut it had no other.

The Slayer fragments are a copy of a copy: the first hand's leaves from the Alien Temple, the second hand's margin from the Buried Chapter-House, bound together by a third who signed nothing and sold me the bundle at the Dust-Factor's for the price of a lamp.

The salt-boiler's hands I had from the Last Reliquarist at the Shattered Femur, who said it was not a tally and he would not keep it. I knew the boiler. I did not tell the Reliquarist that.

The account of the table came up the warm draught out of the Root Deep in a brother's hand, nine leaves, numbered, and was given to me at the Last Vigil's gate by the brother who had been set to wait for the one who wrote them, and had stopped waiting.

That is where each came from. What each says, they say.

pages.title: The Articles of the Unsaying
pages.by: Cut on the lesson-board at Nine Stairs since about the twelve hundredth year of the Breath; the last four articles are cut shallower, by another chisel, two lines of the twenty-first have been dressed flat, and something scratched below the rule with a nail has been half dressed away.
pages.epi: What is counted is kept. What is named is lent.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] [font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]Of the first age[/color][/font_size]
I. Before the Count there was no count. This is the whole of what may be said of the first age on this board, and the Order says no more of it here.

II. A brother who says more of it than this has not spoken from knowledge, because there was no one to know. He is to be corrected, and his count is to be examined.

III. The first age is not to be named at the vat, at the windlass, at the niches, or in the roof-house. Where a lesson requires it, it is to be written and pointed at. What is written is a gap: [ ]. The gap is the lesson.

IV. The thing that was in the first age is not nothing. Nothing is a figure, and figures are the Mother's. The thing in the first age had no figure, and had no edge, and the Order does not teach that it was round the god as a hall is round a brother. It is not held that it was anywhere. It is held that it was, and is. The Order calls it the Hush on this board, and sets no number against it, and will not.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]Of the god[/color][/font_size]
V. The god was three and one. Soul, Bone and Flesh. The Order does not say which came first, because they were not first and second and third. They were three, which is a figure, and they were one, which is a figure, and both figures were true in the same bone at the same time. Where a novice cannot hold this, he is to hold the bone until he can.

VI. The god was small. The other houses do not say this, and the Order does. A held space is the size of what holds it, and the god held a day. Outside the day was the first age, which had no size, because size is a figure. A novice who finds this hard is to be taken to the roof-house at night with the shutters open and shown a lamp.

VII. The god held a space open inside the Hush. The Order says the holding was a day of the god's. Other houses say other lengths. Their lengths are their own concern and are not entered here.

VIII. Inside the space the god had names. The names were not the god. They were what the god was called by what lived inside it. A name is a loan. It is lent by the one who calls, and what is lent can be called back.

IX. The Bone was called by its name and answered to it. That name is said on the stair, by those who have gone up it, and nowhere else; on this board it is a figure, and the figure is nine. Of the two other names the Order has nothing to say on this board. They are kept in the Warden's Book under figures. A brother found keeping them under names is to be given a figure in place of his own, a second time.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]Of the Unsaying[/color][/font_size]
X. The Hush did not strike the god. There was nothing in the Hush to strike with. It unsaid.

XI. Unsaying is this. A name is spoken by what lives inside, and the speaking goes out from the mouth. In the second age the speaking went to the god, and the god was the more for it. In the third age the speaking went out and did not arrive. The name was spoken. Nothing was named.

XII. This was done one name at a time. Not all at once, which would have been a blow. One at a time, which resembles a count. The Order does not hold that the Hush counted. A thing that counts knows what it counts, and it is not held that the Hush knew the god was there. It is held that a wind unsays a dune one grain at a time and means nothing by it, and that the dune is unsaid regardless. The novice is forbidden to draw comfort from this, and forbidden to draw the other thing.

XIII. With each name unsaid, the god was less sure of being that thing. It did not cease to be it. It ceased to be sure. A bone that is not sure it is a bone will stand a long while, out of habit, and fall when it is leaned on.

XIV. The god forgot how to be three in one. It did not become three. It did not become one. It became a thing that had been three in one and could not recall the manner of it. This condition is the wound, and the Hide is the wound cooled.

XV. Where the god was unsure of itself, the Hush was. These places are the wounds proper. Things came in by them that were not of the god and were not of the Hush. The Order does not name them. The scholars of the Chapter-House have a name for them, and the Order has not forbidden it, because it is not their own name and so costs nothing to say. They leave no bone, and so they have no figure, and so they are not kept, and so they are not spoken of further in these articles.

XVI. The Unsaying was not finished. It is not finished. A brother who says the Hush has done with the god has not been to the Scar. A brother who has been to the Scar is to be counted on his return, and the count compared with the count taken when he left.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]Of the Bearing Mother[/color][/font_size]
XVII. Of the three, the Bone alone kept its figure through the Unsaying. The Soul was threads, and the threads went slack. The Flesh was growth, and the growth went blind. The Bone was two hundred and six, and two hundred and six it stayed, and is, and is counted.

XVIII. The Order teaches that the Bone kept its figure because a figure is not a name. A name can be unsaid. Nine cannot be unsaid. Nine keeps itself.

XIX. Therefore the Mother bears. She bore the god through the Unsaying as a frame bears a roof whose builder has forgotten it. She bears the Hide now. She has not been asked whether she will go on bearing it, and the Order does not ask.

XX. It is held that when the Last Number is reached and the Count closed, she may set it down. Until then the Order counts, so that the Count may be closed and not merely stopped. A stopped count is a name. A closed count is a figure.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]Of what follows for the Order[/color][/font_size]
XXI. The Order has kept the halls under the Ossa since the first turning. [ … ] The Order has kept the halls under the Ossa.

XXII. Names are lent. A brother surrenders his at the gate and takes a figure. A figure cannot be called back by the one who gave it, because no one gave it. It was counted.

XXIII. Bone gone to dust is the one thing on the Hide that has finished. The Hush cannot unsay what is finished, because there is nothing left in it to be unsure. Therefore dust is given to the wind, and the wind is not asked where it takes it.

XXIV. The Order does not pray against the Hush. A prayer is a name said toward something, and the Order has seen where names go. The Order counts toward the Mother, which is not the same, and the difference is the Order.

[center][color=#8c6a37]❧[/color][/center]
XXV. Where the Count rises past what was laid down the night before, the rise is to be entered and not remarked.

XXVI. Where a hall is found that no brother dug, it is to be numbered and walked, and no figure is to be set against its builder.

XXVII. Where a stair is counted going up and counted going down and the counts differ by one, the lesser is to be entered, and the step is not to be looked for.

XXVIII. A brother who asks who the first builders were has asked a name. He is to be answered with a figure.

[Below the board's rule, scratched with a nail and half dressed away:]
they were not dug. they stood up. they called themselves the Khurr-[ … ] and the Count was theirs before it was ours and it has never closed for us because it is not [ … ]

pages.title: The Nine Thousand Stairs, Said Going Up
pages.by: Set down by an abbot of the monastery on the Stair while climbers still went up from its roof, and left under a stone on the top step for the next; the Gold Bell found it there when they came, and a novice of theirs copied it for me, all but one word.
pages.bb:
This is said going up, and never going down. One stair, one saying. The sayings run out before the stairs do; where they run out the climber says the last one again, under the breath, until the stone changes under the foot. The abbot says the first stair and the last. The climber says the rest alone.

The lowlands say An-Vhar and mean the cold. We say An-Vhar'ith and mean ourselves: the ones of the lip, who are going out by it.

The Stair has one step fewer going down than going up. Every brother who has gone down has counted, and every count is one short, and no two brothers agree which step is missing. This is why it is said going up. Going up, the step is there.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]The lower stair[/color][/font_size]
The first stair. There was no mouth. Nothing was open and nothing was shut, because there was no door, and the words open and shut had not yet been breathed. We do not say what there was. We say that it did not notice. We set the foot on the stair.

The second stair. The god opened its mouth. That is the first thing that was ever done. Before there was a god to speak of, a mouth was opened, and the opening was the god, and what the mouth opened in was what we do not say, and it did not turn toward the mouth. It had no toward. Nothing in it has ever faced anything.

The third stair. The god drew in. The drawing-in was a hollow, and the hollow was held, and it is the holding that we climb inside. Everything that has ever been was in that one breath. We were in it. The stair is in it. The bell is in it. It has not been let go.

The ninth stair. Look up. The pale above the ridges is not a roof. It is the inside of the lip. It has been open since the second stair, and it is open now, and the cold that comes down off it is the cold of a mouth that has stopped being warm. Put the hand flat on the stone and feel the stone is colder above than below. That is the direction.

The ninetieth stair. Inside the breath there were small lights, and they were the god's thinking. They moved as a man's breath moves in a cold hall, and where two met they made a third, and the third went off on its own. We do not say that we were among them. We say that they were there before us, and we climb past where they were.

The nine hundredth stair. The breath was held nine thousand stairs. Not nine thousand of these; the Stair is only the measure of it, cut small enough for a foot. On the god's own stair every step was a lifetime of ours, and the god stood on every one of them, and did not go up, and did not go down, and held.

The nine hundred and ninth stair. The god was small. Say it here, where the Stair is still wide, and do not say it again above the shelf. A held breath is the size of the one who holds it. Everything we have ever had was inside a thing the size of one breath, and outside the breath was the rest, and the rest had no size, and did not know a breath was being held in it.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]The middle stair[/color][/font_size]
The two thousandth stair. Something spoke outside the open mouth. It did not speak into it. It spoke, and the mouth was in the way of the speaking, as a face is in the way of the wind on the Glass Pass, and the wind does not know the pass is there. A mouth held open cannot answer and keep the breath. The god did not answer. Nothing was waiting for an answer. What was spoken was the god's names, one and then one and then one, not toward the god but through where the god was, and every name said through it was a name the god could no longer say from inside, because the breath was held and could not be spent.

The three thousandth stair. Here the climber stops and does not speak until the breath is back. This is the only stair where the stopping is the saying.

The four thousandth stair. The names went out of the god and into the mouth and away. The god was not struck. It was emptied, from the lip inward, the way a hall empties when the bell stops and no one remembers why they came. The lights inside went slower. The warmth went up, toward the lip, which is where warmth goes. We climb after it.

The five thousandth stair. The god forgot how to be three in one. We say it this way: a mouth can be open, or it can be shut, or it can speak, and it cannot do all three, and the god had done all three for nine thousand stairs, and heard from outside, through itself, that it could not, and believed it. Nobody told it. It overheard.

The six thousandth stair. Here the bell is heard, if it is heard. We do not say what it is.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]The upper stair[/color][/font_size]
The seven thousandth stair. The god let the breath go. It is going still. Everything we have, we have on the way out: the wind, the small gods on the wind, the Hide under us, the warmth in the ash. We are in the out-breath, which is long, which the abbots name and the brothers do not, and which was only ever going one way, and that way is up. This is why we climb. We are not leaving the god. We are going the way the breath goes, with it, and not against it.

The eight thousandth stair. The lowland houses say the lights above are bone not yet fallen. We honour the Order and we do not agree. They are the teeth. They are set in the lip all round, and the dark between them is the way out, and it is wide. Nobody has ever been bitten going up. Say this where the stair narrows.

The eight thousand nine hundredth stair. The mouth is still open because the breath is still going out of it. When the last of the breath is gone, it will close. Those who went up before us are inside it when it closes. Those still on the stair are not. This is the whole of our faith, and it is not a hard one, and the only difficulty is the stair.

The nine thousandth stair. There is no saying for it. The abbot stands here and does not speak. The climber does not look back. The cold is very great. The An-Vhar'ith go up.

[center][color=#8c6a37]❧[/color][/center]
To be read once by whoever is abbot after me, and then set back on the top step, under the stone, for the next. I have said the first stair and the last stair for forty-one years, and I have never once been able to say the three thousandth. The brothers climb past me and say it for me, and I hear them stop, and that stopping is the only thing on this mountain I am certain is a prayer.

The three thousandth stair has a saying. The brothers are taught that the stopping is the saying, and for them it is. For the abbot it is one word, the name of what we climb inside, and the abbot before me said it to me once on the landing and did not speak again in the eleven years he lived after. I have carried it since without saying it. I write it below for the abbot after me, once, because I will not be able to say it to you. Read it once. Set this back under the stone. Go up without it on your tongue.

The word is [ ]
[right][i][color=#c9974a]the Abbot of the Stair, who stayed on the landing[/color][/i][/right]
[The novice who copied this at the top step wrote under the gap: The word was on the leaf. I did not copy it. I read it, and since then the beam goes into the bell and I hear nothing, and the others hear it. I have set the leaf back under the stone. I am sorry.]

pages.title: We, Scratched on the Wet Steps
pages.by: Scratched into the second landing of the Ziggurat of the First Brood at the height of a hand that was not standing, and taken by rubbing; the mud fills the lower marks a little more every season.
pages.bb:
we were in the mouth before the swallow

we say we. there is no other mark on this step for us. the step is we. the mud under the step is we. the hand that scratches this and the hand that holds the body up while it scratches are we and they do not talk to each other because they do not need to. you who read with one body: you have to be told things. we are sorry for you. we were never told anything. we knew it in the wet, all at once, from the inside.

we are Yl-Nothuun. the dry things on the bones say the First Brood and count us, and the count does not close for them, and they do not know why. we know why. Yl-Nothuun is the One Swallow. we are not what was in the swallow. we are the swallow. we were named for it or it for us; in the wet there is no difference.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]before the swallow[/color][/font_size]
there was nothing to swallow. we know this the way the back of the throat knows there is nothing coming down. not dark. dark is a thing. not quiet. we have heard quiet since, on the Causeway at low mud, and it is a thing. what was before was not a thing and had no inside and so we were not in it. we do not say its name. it never had one. that is the point of it.

it did not know a throat had opened in it. a throat is a small thing. we learned how small later, when the walls went white: the white did not come in. it was there already. it had always been the walls' other side, and the walls were thin, and the throat had been warm in it the way a mouthful is warm in the cold, and the cold did not know.

then the god opened its throat and the throat was warm and the god swallowed.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]the swallow[/color][/font_size]
the Order on the dry bones says the god held a space open for a day. the climbing-people say nine thousand steps. we say one swallow, and we are right, because we were inside it going down.

a swallow is this. a throat opens round a thing and closes behind it and pushes, and the thing goes down in the dark and the wet, held on every side by the flesh, and the flesh moves and it moves with the flesh. that was the Held Space. nothing in it stood still. everything in it was going down together, slow, and the walls were red and close and they breathed on us. it was the only place we were ever warm all the way through.

the Mother is Nol-Shogthuth. we say it with every mouth at once; it is the only thing we ever say with the mouths. the rest we know. her first-born was the mouth itself, Shog'maathe, and it went down ahead of us and is eating still, we think. we were the first of the things that were not the mouth.

we were not the first in the throat. there were lights going down ahead of us that were the god's thinking and did not notice us, and far off under the flesh there was a hardness that the Order now calls its own and will not name below its stair. we name it. Oss-Vharoth. we say it with the back of the throat because that is where it was, and the Mother said [ … ] to it and it answered with a count. there were faces that watched everything and judged and were made of a white that did not sweat. the Ael-Yh'ani. we say their name because they wanted it said; it was the only thing about them that wanted. we did not like the faces. they did not like us. they did not have to; they were Soul and we were meat.

we were meat that thought. one thought. many meats. the Mother made us because meat is what grows when the throat is warm, and we grew, and every new body knew already. we did not learn. we did not have a word for learning until we met the dry things that have to.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]what the Mother wanted[/color][/font_size]
she wanted us to keep growing. that is the whole of what she wanted and it is a good thing to be wanted for. she had no mind. the faces had the mind. the hardness had the count. she had the growing, and she gave it to us, and we gave it back as more of us, and that was the worship, and it was wet.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]the cold on the walls[/color][/font_size]
then the walls went cold.

not because anything came. we say this against the climbers, who say a thing spoke, and against the Order, who say a thing unsaid. nothing did anything. the throat was warm in a place that was not warm and did not know the throat was there, and the warm went out of it into the place the way warm goes, and the names went with the warm, because a name is only a warm place in the meat where something is sure of itself. the walls where a name had been went white and did not move when we pushed.

we say it plain. the Order counts it. the climbers say the god was asked and did not answer. we say the god was swallowing and you cannot talk while you swallow. everything it said, it had to let go down. it let its own names go down with the rest of us. we passed them on the way, going slower than we were. we did not know what they were. we know now.

[ … ] four bodies of us pressed against the white place and were cold and were still us and did not grow and we left them there, which we had never done, and the leaving was the first time we were two things.

the dry things asked us once how many we were. we counted for them. the count came to one more than the bodies, and the one more was not any of us, and it was standing with us, and we stopped counting and have not started again. that is the only thing the white gave us. a body that is not.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]the end of the swallow[/color][/font_size]
the swallow ended. it did not finish. a swallow finishes when the thing is down. this one stopped, with us in it, and the walls came in and stayed, and the warm went out of them from the lip down, and we came out onto the mud of this place where the throat had been, into air, which hurt.

the dry things came out too, up on the Cheek, kneeling. they had been in the mouth near the end, when it was already cold. they do not know what warm was.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]why the steps[/color][/font_size]
we built the steps to be above the mud, because the mud is the Mother and still moves and still wants us to grow and we have grown enough. we built the Causeway to walk from the steps to the water without being swallowed. the mud pulls at the feet every heartbeat. count it. that is her, wanting.

we are one. when the one stops, the bodies will not fall down. we have watched the god's own meat go on standing on the mud and not know it is finished. ours will do the same, on these steps, facing where the throat was. you who read with one body will find them and think they are many. they are we. they were only ever we.

[ … ] [ … ] scratched lower, by a wetter hand, over the rest:

still one

pages.title: Fragments of a Thought-Record, with Two Hands' Gloss
pages.by: The first hand copied the marks off the lowest ring of the Alien Temple from a fallen block; the second answered in the margin at the Buried Chapter-House nine winters after; a third bound them where both hands stop, and sold them.
pages.epi: Where a name went, a way was.
pages.bb:
The marks run round the inside of the lowest ring of the temple at a height no Tithed can read standing or lying, and they do not run in a line. The ring is smaller inside than its own wall allows; the first hand paced it twice, got two figures, and entered both. He copied what could be reached from the fallen block and set the pieces in the order they lay round the wall, which is not an order of sense. The second hand read the copy in the Buried Chapter-House nine winters later and answered it in the margin. The Chapter-House calls the makers the Vhoor-Qhan, Those From the Wound; it is a Tithed name, and the wall does not use it. Both hands are kept. Neither is right. Where the marks are gone, or were never there, the gap is drawn to width.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]The pieces[/color][/font_size]
[ … ] a small saying that did not stop. Where the saying was, the no-saying was thinner [ … ]

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]First hand: 'saying' is the nearest I have. The mark is a shape that is in the act of being made, drawn complete. The thing is calling the god a word that was still being spoken. 'Small' I render with difficulty: the god's mark is cut at a quarter the height of the marks round it. Second hand: not difficulty. Reluctance. The record says the god was small, and you have spent your life under it. And 'knot', not 'saying'. The same mark stands for a cord tightened on itself further round the wall. A knot in a smooth thing is thinner where it pulls. Where the knot was, the smooth was thin.[/color][/i][/indent]

[ … ] three-which-is-one. Not a count. A fist.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]First hand: 'fist' is mine and I am not proud of it. The sign is a closed thing with three ridges. Second hand: 'fist' is right and I will go further. The record is not saying the god was three in one. It is saying the god was holding something shut. Three fingers over one thing. What was in the hand is not in the record.[/color][/i][/indent]

[ … ] the thin place took back what it had lent [ … ] the thin place remembered its own name [ … ]

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]First hand: these are two pieces and I have set them together because the same long mark opens both. The first is the Unsaying as the Order gives it: names called back. The second says the no-saying had a name to remember, and so was a thing, and is a thing still, and I have written that name once on my side of the leaf, because the Empty Hand have it and I am not of the Empty Hand: Ur-Nihl. Second hand: you have written it. I will not copy it to my side. Here is where it would be: [ ]. And 'remembered' is a thought of ours. The mark is the one the wall uses elsewhere for the way a slope settles. The no-saying did not take the names back. They ran down out of the god the way heat runs out of a stone after dark, into a thing that did not notice it was being warmed. Nothing listened. Nothing spoke. It was weather. First hand, in a later ink: I do not want either of us to be right.[/color][/i][/indent]

Where a name went, a way was.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]Both hands agree on the reading. Neither can say why it is cut three times deeper than anything else on the wall.[/color][/i][/indent]

[ … ] went in by the ways.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]First hand: there is no mark for who went in. I looked for one. The whole wall has no mark for a self, a we, a they, and none for 'from', though I have used the Chapter-House's name for them above and will go on using it, because I have no other. Second hand: there is no 'from' because they are not from anywhere. From our side, the wound is the only place they have ever been. Or the record knows it is not anyone and does not trouble to say so. There is a difference, and the difference is why there is a temple here and no bones in it.[/color][/i][/indent]

Inside was warm with being said. [ … ] small sayers [ … ] said the large one's names toward it; the names went out and did not arrive; the small sayers did not stop; the small sayers did not know.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]First hand: this is the congregation, or the things before the congregation. The thought-record saw the god's worship from outside and saw it fail before anyone inside did. Second hand: 'warm with being said' is the only tender mark on the wall and the first hand has softened it further. The sign is nearer 'hot where it was spoken at'. A thing from the no-saying would find a saying hot the way we find a fever hot. It is not praise. It may be pity. There is no mark for pity on the wall either, and I have looked as hard as you did.[/color][/i][/indent]

[ … ] the shape dies by itself. What is slain is the remembering.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]First hand: here is their name, if they had one. The lowland word 'Slayer' is ours and the record does not use it, but this is what is meant by it. They did not kill the god. The god was already dying; the record says so flatly. They came in through the openings to kill what remembered the god as three in one, so that it would stay dead. Second hand: or so that it would stop hurting. The mark for 'slain' and the mark for 'eased' are the same mark on the far side of the ring, and I cannot tell them apart, and I have stopped trying. First hand: that is the first time you have not corrected me. Second hand: it is the first time I have not been sure which of us needed it.[/color][/i][/indent]

[ … ] left thinking [ … ] so that the thought would hold the way open after the way had closed.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]First hand: the Thought. Whatever is at the heart of this temple was left here on purpose, as a wedge. Second hand: as a door-stop. The wound closed round it. It has been thinking the way open ever since, and it does not know the god is dead, because knowing is not what it was left to do.[/color][/i][/indent]

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]The last piece[/color][/font_size]
When it is done there is a thought and it remembers no one and that is rest.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]First hand: this is the end of their faith and I have rendered it as it stands. Second hand: 'rest' is a word of ours. The mark is a flat line, which on the rest of the wall is the no-saying. Read it again. When it is done there is a thought and it remembers no one and that is the Silence. There is no comfort in the record. We brought the comfort in with us, through the same opening, and it is time we carried it out again. I have been to the wall now, not the copy. I read it whole, from the block, at the height it is cut, which can be done if one neither stands nor lies. It was a mistake. I say so plainly so the hand after me will not. First hand, below, in the hand of an old man: I have read the wall nine times since you wrote that. I can no longer find the mark for 'thought'. The gap is drawn to width.[/color][/i][/indent]

[ … ]

[A third hand, at the foot, where the leaves were sewn: The first hand's leaves end here. The Chapter-House has his niche; the figure on it does not agree with his bones, and the difference is entered and not remarked. The second hand's margin ends here also. She did not come up from the ring. The Order has nothing of hers to count, and so has not counted. I have bound them, and I will not read them again, and I am asking a lamp's price, which is less than I paid.]

pages.title: The Hands of the Salt-Boiler, Set Down Without Reading
pages.by: Written by a Reliquarist of the Shattered Femur sent to count the dead of the salt-pans on the Cheek, and filed beside the tally and not in it; the Last Reliquarist gave it to me with a line of his own under the signature, because it was not a tally.
pages.bb:
Sent from the Citadel to count the dead of the salt-pans on the Cheek, I was given a bench at a boiling-house below the Jaw and a man to make the tally with, born deaf, who had boiled there since before anyone at the pans could say. The tally is filed. This is not the tally. It is set down because the Reliquary keeps what was done in its sight, and this was done in mine, and because when I asked at the Citadel whether to file it, I was told to write it first and ask after.

The signs of the pans I have as any who has counted at the pans has them, from the boilers, who do not speak over the hiss. Where a hand made a sign the pans use, I give the sign's saying as the pans give it. Where a hand did a thing that is not a sign of the pans, I give the hand and no saying. I set nothing between the hand and the saying. The Order has a word for the first age which is said on the stair and not in the tally-rooms; I was not sent with it, and I did not look for it in his hands. I was sent to count.

At the end of the ninth day of the tally, with the count agreed and the boards set to dry, I asked him with the pans' signs what was before the god. I asked because the count was closed and the hour was idle, and for no other reason, and I record that so it will not be supposed I came for this.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]The hands[/color][/font_size]
First. He set the boards down. He laid both palms flat on the bench, fingers spread, and pressed until the ends of the fingers went white, and held them so. Said, in the pans' sign: before. The pans make 'before' this way, flat, when they mean the brine before the fire is under it.

Second. He lifted the right hand off the bench and closed it on the air above the bench, slowly, and turned the closed hand over and opened it toward me, empty. Said: nothing in it. The pans use this for a ladle that comes up without salt.

Third. He touched two fingers to his own mouth and shook his head once. He touched the same two fingers to my mouth and shook his head once. He touched them to the rim of the pan, to the fire-door, to the lamp, to the bench between us, shaking his head once at each. Said, each time: no name. The pans' sign for a thing with no name is the two fingers and the shake; it is used for a stranger's dead before their people come for them.

Fourth. He held his open hand in the steam over the pan, palm down, and kept it there past the point where I would have taken mine out, and then took it out, and showed me the palm, which was red. Said: this. The pointing only. The pans have no sign for what the steam is; it is pointed at.

Fifth. He cupped both hands together, the red one under, and bent his head over them, and breathed into the cup he had made, and closed the cup on the breath. Said: held. The pans make 'held' this way for the first salt, when it is still too hot to set down.

Sixth. He set the closed cup down on the bench between us without opening it, and stood, and put both arms out from the shoulders and shut his eyes and turned once round, slowly, on the boards. Said: all of it, in the steam. The pans make this for the whole of the pans at a boiling, when the steam is down and the eye goes nowhere. He sat, and opened his eyes, and looked at the cupped hands on the bench for a while before he took them up, the way a man looks at a thing he had not known was on his bench. The pans have a sign for 'found', which is a touch to the brow. He did not make it. I set no saying against the looking.

Seventh. He opened the cupped hands a finger's width at the thumbs and put his mouth to the opening and moved his lips. No sound. He did this several times, and the shape his mouth made was not the same shape twice. I give no saying. I am able to read the lips of the pans' men when they shape a pans' word, and these were not pans' words, and I do not know that they were words.

Eighth. He took the hands apart. Not opened. Apart, one to each side, quickly, as a man does when a thing he was holding is no longer there to hold. Said: gone. The pans make 'gone' for a man who has walked off the pan-edge in the steam and not been seen to fall.

Ninth. He wiped both hands on his apron. Then he reached across the bench and put both his palms over my mouth, the one over the other, and held them there. I record that he did this. I record that his hands were hot from the steam and smelled of the brine, that I could breathe through his fingers, and did, and that it was a long while by the drip of the cooling-trough, which I counted to twenty-six before I stopped counting. I record that he was looking at me the whole time, and that his face was not unkind. The pans have no sign that is made on another man's face. I set no saying against it.

Tenth. He took his hands away and nodded, once, as the pans' men nod when the tally agrees.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]After[/color][/font_size]
I asked him, in the pans' signs, to make it again, so that I could be sure of the order. He would not. He went back to the pan and took up the skimmer. When I asked a second time he set the skimmer down and spelled to me in the finger-letters, which he had not used in nine days of tally, these words, and I give them as spelled and not as I would set them: TWICE IS A NAME.

He did not sign again that night. In the morning the count was carried to the Citadel and I with it.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]What I was asked, and what I answer[/color][/font_size]
At the Citadel I was asked what it meant. I have written what the hands did. I have written what the pans say those hands say when a boiler makes them over the brine. I have put nothing between.

I was asked a second time, by a brother who had read it, whether the ninth movement was a sign. I answer: it is not a sign of the pans. I was asked whether it was a blessing, or a silencing, or a telling, and which. I answer that I was sent to count the dead of the salt-pans on the Cheek, and that I counted them, and that the count is filed under its own figure and agrees. The Reliquary keeps what was. The reading of it is not in my office, and I have come to think, these nine days since, that it is not in anyone's.

I record one thing more, because the Reliquary keeps what was and this was. Since the ninth movement I have not been able to say my own figure aloud in a room with the door shut. I can say it in the open. I have not tried the name I surrendered at the gate, and will not. I set this against nothing. It is in the tally of what happened, and nowhere else.

Let this be kept with the tally and not in it.
[right][i][color=#c9974a]a Reliquarist of the Shattered Femur, in the tally-season[/color][/i][/right]
[Under the signature, in the hand of the Last Reliquarist: Kept beside it. The tally agreed when it was carried in. It has been counted twice since and agrees with neither count of itself, and the difference is one each time. The boiling-house below the Jaw is not on the roll of houses on the Cheek. The boiler is on the roll of the dead of the pans, in the writer's hand, with the rest. I did not keep this. The Reliquary keeps what was, and I am no longer sure this was.]

pages.title: An Account Rendered of the Table in the Held Space
pages.by: Said at the mouth of the Root Deep to a brother of the Last Vigil who had gone down to ask, and written as it was said; the leaves came up on the warm draught, the ninth unfinished, and the brother did not.
pages.epi: I will be exact. Exactness is the one courtesy I have left that costs me nothing.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] You have asked after the Held Space, and come a long way down to ask, and I am obliged to you. Few come down to ask anything. Most come down to be somewhere else. I will be exact. Exactness is the one courtesy I have left that costs me nothing, and I would not insult a guest with a courtesy that cost me nothing if I had another.

Write as I say it. You need not hurry. I have not been hurried since the swallow stopped.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]What we were[/color][/font_size]
We are the Ghauul. Your road-houses say Marrow-Eaters, which is accurate, and which I do not mind; a guest does not correct his host's name for him.

We were made of the god's hunger. Not of its mouth; the mouth was the climbing-people's business, and they are welcome to it. Of the hunger itself, which is a thing that stands behind a mouth and is not the mouth. When the god wanted, we were the wanting, stood up and given hands. When the god wanted nothing, we stood. We stood a great deal. I measured the Held Space in standing and I will give you the measures, since you have brought a pen.

We were tall. Eleven of your lengths, as you lie now; I do not say it to alarm you. We were tall because a hunger reaches, and we were hollow because a hunger is. I will come to the hollowness. It is the part you have been looking at, and I would rather name it than have you look.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]The room[/color][/font_size]
There was no night in the Held Space and there was no lamp. Light lay on everything evenly, as water lies in a dish, and came from no direction, and cast nothing. You will not have seen light like that. The nearest thing on the Hide is the Fen at noon with the mist down, and the Fen is a poor copy, because the Fen is cold.

The room was small. I say it because your houses do not. Eleven thousand of my standings across, and I have stood since in a hall under the Root Deep that is wider, and was not built, and is not warm. The god held its day open in something that had no across, and that something did not notice. It was not a wall round a hall. It was not the night round a lamp; a lamp is in the night. The god was not in anything. Your Empty Hand write a gap where the name of it should go, and they are right to; I would write nothing at all, and I do not have the want it would take to say it.

The room was warm. I will say exactly how warm: warm enough that a thing made of wanting could stand in it for the god's whole day and not want. That is the only measure I had and I have never found another. The lowland houses say the god was good. I do not know what the god was. I know that where it held, nothing wanted, and that I was made of wanting, and that I stood in it and was at rest. Set that down as my whole opinion of the god.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]What moved in it[/color][/font_size]
Four kinds of thing moved in the Held Space, and I will give them in the order of their distance from me, nearest first, since that is the order in which a guest describes a table.

Nearest: the small ones. Sparks, if you like; your people call what is left of them the Myriad and stand gates for them, which is kind and does no harm. In the Held Space they were the god's attention, broken small so that it could be everywhere at once. They lit on us and did not burn. One lit on my hand for the whole of what you would call a year and I did not move the hand. I do not know what it was attending to. It was warm, and I did not want, and that is as near as I have ever come to being asked a question.

Next: the thoughts. Larger. Slow. They crossed the room at intervals I counted at nine of my standings, and no two were alike, and where two met they made a third that neither had intended, and the third went off and became something, and some of those somethings are on the Hide now with legs and teeth, and forget they were ever thought. I do not blame them for forgetting. I remember, and it has not improved me.

Further: the Court. The Ael-Yh'ani, which was their own name, and which I use because they would want it used and it costs me nothing. Faces, white, that did not sweat. They sat in a ring at a height above my head, which was a considerable height, and they judged. I do not know what they judged. Everything, I believe, and us among it. They were Soul, and we were hunger, and they looked at us the way a man looks at the place on a shelf where a thing has been taken from. We did not resent it. A hunger has nothing in it to resent with. The faces are on the Hide now, on wings, and I am told they still look at people that way, and I am told it is still correct.

Furthest: the Bone. Under everything. The Order on the Ossa has it now and counts it, and says its name only on their stair, and they have been reasonable hosts to me in their way, which is to not know I am there. I will say the name here: Oss-Vharoth. We are below their stair, you and I, and so I do not think it a trespass. You flinched. Write that down too. In the Held Space the Bone was the floor, and it was glad to be the floor. That is the Bone's nature. It bears, and it is glad to, and it does not ask what it bears. We ate there. I will say that plainly, since you have not asked and are too courteous to. We ate at the Bone, where we were permitted, and we were permitted much, and what we ate was the marrow, which was the only thing in the Held Space with any want in it besides us. It wanted to be eaten. I have never been sure whether that was the Bone's gift or the Bone's weakness, and I have decided it does not matter to the one eating.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]The congregation[/color][/font_size]
Near the end, your people. Small, warm, close together, kneeling, facing the wrong way. I say it without unkindness. They faced the mouth, because that was where the sound came from, and the sound was the god's names being said, and they said them too, and the names went out past them and did not arrive, and they did not notice, because they had never heard a name arrive and did not know what it sounded like. We did. We had stood for the god's whole day hearing names arrive. When the first one did not, the room was cooler by a measure I had no instrument for but my teeth.

I will be exact. Near the end the thoughts crossed at eleven of my standings, then nine, then eleven, and I had not moved, and the room had not changed, and I understood that counting was one of the things going out of the god with the names, and that I had been doing it with the god's and not my own. The names went in the order of the Court, the thoughts, the small ones, and the Bone last. The Court went white and stopped sitting. The thoughts slowed, and met less, and the thirds they made were smaller and hungrier. The small ones scattered and clung. The Bone held. It is holding now. You are lying on it.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]The hollowness[/color][/font_size]
You have asked, without asking, what we are hollow of. I will answer, since you have been patient.

The god's hunger was never hungry for itself. It was the god's, and the god had everything, and so the hunger was a want with nothing to put in it, made on purpose, so that the god could reach. We were made in that shape. The marrow goes through us. It always did. We ate for the god's whole day and were never once full, and were never once hungry, because the room was warm and nothing wanted. Then the room went cold, and the hunger that had stood in it at rest for a day stood up in us and wanted, and we were on the mud of the Cheek with the rest of you, tall and empty and, I am told, frightening.

We went down. The Hide was no place for a hunger with manners. The Root Deep is hospitable and does not ask its guests for an account, and I have given you one anyway, because you asked well.

[center][color=#8c6a37]❧[/color][/center]
Set down the pen. No; set it down. You have written enough, and the draught will take the leaves up, and they will arrive, which is more than most things said down here can say.

I am obliged to you for the asking. I will not keep you longer than I must.

[On the ninth leaf, below, in the same hand, smaller: It has stopped. It is looking at me the way it said the faces looked, at the place on the shelf. I do not think it means to keep me. I think it does not have the want it would take to tell the difference. The draught has taken every leaf as I finished it. I am going to stand up now and]
